action: Organisations that send texts through CSCTelecom: ask what of your traffic was exposed and whether it was accessed. Old one-time codes have expired, but warn customers about scams that reference past messages. No action is needed by most individuals.
date_note: Reported in a Nov 6-12 roundup; exact disclosure day not confirmed
exec: A messaging supplier's exposed database leaked years of one-time codes and sensitive texts; the gap is closed but past exposure remains.
impact: Over 125 million text messages were exposed. That is a count of messages, not of people.
plain: A database belonging to telecom firm CSCTelecom was left open, exposing over 125 million text messages sent from October 2022 to September 2026, including bank login codes and emergency-line messages. It has since been secured.
summary: An exposed database of CSCTelecom's Latvian branch leaked over 125 million SMS messages sent between October 2022 and September 2026, including bank authentication codes and messages to the national emergency hotline. CSCTelecom acknowledged a vulnerability and says it is fixed (as relayed by a roundup of Cybernews reporting).
title: CSCTelecom database exposed 125 million SMS messages

validation.note: One roundup; exact disclosure day unknown.

review.note: Roundup says 'over 125 million' SMS; record said about 125 million; fixed in impact, plain, summary. Single aggregator source (original Cybernews not read), so status rests on the roundup relaying the company's acknowledgement
